# How to make videos with Claude Fable 5.2: Blender films, game trailers, 3D explainers and Fable vs Opus

**Turn one prompt into a video made of code: a Blender film written in Python, a trailer of a game the model built, a 3D explainer or a Fable vs Opus split screen.**

**Price:** free on the main route, with no API key. Optional paid steps on the varg API: `video-sound` (~$0.01–0.02 per voice line, $0.01–0.06 per sound effect, $0.05 per 20 s music bed; mixing free).

<p><a href="../../blender-code-film/README.md"><img src="https://s3.varg.ai/files/4325c578-378d-4c43-ae53-3cc3218df1ea/file_417a3b4d8684.webp" alt="A low-poly forest valley at dusk rendered in Blender from Python: a glowing lantern orb drifts between pine trees through warm haze and floating sparks." width="480"></a></p>

**Short answer:** start with [`blender-code-film`](../../blender-code-film/README.md): a short film in Blender written entirely in Python: shots as data, stills first, critic loop, Eevee or Cycles, music bed. The other 6 skills below add the steps around it. Ask your agent for the result in your own words; it asks the few choices that matter before anything is paid for and hands back the files.

```bash
# Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot, OpenCode and other agents
npx skills add vargHQ/skills --skill blender-code-film --skill code-game-trailer --skill code-3d-explainer --skill model-split-screen --skill code-to-video-previz --skill video-sound --skill code-path-traced-film
```

Then ask your agent in plain words, for example: *"Make a 20-second low-poly storybook film in Blender, entirely in Python: a lantern drifting through a forest at dusk, 4 shots. Stills first."*

## Requests to paste into your agent

- "Make a 20-second low-poly storybook film in Blender, entirely in Python: a lantern drifting through a forest at dusk, 4 shots. Stills first."
- "I built a browser game in ./game/index.html. Record a 20-second trailer with 5 shots, a title card and an end card."
- "Make a 3D explainer of how a mitochondrion makes energy, built one part at a time, with a fact sheet I can check first."
- "Same prompt to Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5: lay out both results side by side with their time and cost, 9:16, blind until the last 3 seconds."

## What you need

- The generation steps call the [varg API](https://varg.ai) (Seedance, Kling, Veo, GPT Image, ElevenLabs and more on one key). Sign in to the varg MCP with OAuth or set `VARG_API_KEY`. Models are billed at provider price, 1 credit = $0.01, and the agent shows an estimate before anything expensive.
- `video-sound`: ~$0.01–0.02 per voice line, $0.01–0.06 per sound effect, $0.05 per 20 s music bed; mixing free.
- Any agent that reads Agent Skills: Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot, OpenCode and others ([install options](../../README.md#install)).

## FAQ

### Does Claude Fable 5.2 generate video?

Not as a video model. It writes code that renders video: Python that drives Blender, three.js or WebGL scenes recorded in headless Chrome, or HyperFrames compositions. These skills give it the rendering, recording and checking steps that make the result a finished MP4.

### Do I need a GPU or a paid key?

No. Eevee renders the 9-second starter film at 1080p in about 11 minutes on an Apple Silicon Mac, and the game and explainer captures run in headless Chrome. A varg key is only needed for an optional music bed or narration.

### How do people make the Fable vs Opus side-by-side videos?

Run one prompt twice under the same rules in fresh sessions, log time and cost while each runs, trim both to the same moment, then model-split-screen lays them out with the numbers under each clip, optionally blind until the reveal.

### Why record a game with a virtual clock instead of a screen recorder?

A screen recorder drops frames whenever the machine is busy. With the page's clock replaced, every frame is rendered on purpose at 30 or 60 fps, so the trailer is smooth and the same on every run, and scripted inputs and cameras make each shot repeatable.

### How do I keep a 3D science film accurate?

code-3d-explainer writes a fact sheet with a source for every claim and has a fresh critic check it before any 3D work. A 586k-view launch-day film about atoms was called out in replies for the wrong physics.
